comment: Order of work chosen by the owner (2026-10-07): UI first, then desktop integration, then rendering and media, then 3D and WebGL, then everything else, then (a group marked last) the cross builds and simulators the owner asked to leave for the end. tools/next-task takes the first group with a startable task; inside a group the ordinal decides. A task goes to the first group that matches (milestone, label, or a regex on the title). 2026-10-09: performance moved first (owner), games and the handheld/board milestones placed before the deferred group. 2026-10-10 (owner): the development Mac first; ARM, Pi, ESP32, Linux, handhelds and CHIP go to the cross-platform pass at the end. 2026-10-10 evening (owner): two showcase demos first (M27). 2026-10-10 evening: the whole order was reviewed (docs/reports/backlog-review-2026-10-10.md): after the showcase demos, every task that can be worked on the Mac is in one list, in ordinal order (rank x 1000); the cross-platform pass is one group at the end. A new task is created without an ordinal and so queues at the end of the Mac list until the next review, unless it is a defect that stops a demo. Owner's answers the same evening: a performance follow-up queues at the end like any other task (every ms stays measured and logged); mobile stays in the cross-platform pass; after the showcase demos the free parallel agents take the JS library lane (three.js, Phaser, p5.js, PixiJS).
